records.title: George Russell makes new announcement after Brazilian Grand Prix
records.excerpt: George Russell makes new announcement after Brazilian Grand Prix New George Russell announcement as karting academy launched Oliver Harden 12 Nov 2026 12:07 PM Mercedes driver George Russell faces the media at the 2026 Brazilian Grand Prix Mercedes driver George Russell has launched a new karting academy to help identify and develop emerging motorsport talent. Russell says the GR63 Karting Academy, launched in collaboration with the Silverstone circuit, has been created “to give something back” to motorsport and help break down the financial barriers facing youngsters. George Russell launches GR63 Karting Academy The GR63 Karting Academy, based at Kart Silverstone, is open to boys and girls aged eight and nine with the aim of making karting accessible to talented youngsters from all backgrounds. The process will be split into four stages, starting with open-access arrive-and-drive qualifiers held at Silverstone throughout December. The best 80 drivers will progress to step two, the GR63 shootout, in January 2027. Russell himself will identify the best 25 drivers to compete in the GR63 Championship, a fully funded eight-round season staged at Kart Silverstone between March and November. The top five drivers in the championship will go head to head in a final assessment at Silverstone in December 2027, with the winner receiving a fully funded karting season in 2028. George Russell vs Kimi Antonelli: Mercedes head-to-head stats for F1 2026 season F1 2026: Head-to-head qualifying statistics between teammates F1 2026: Head-to-head race statistics between teammates Russell said: “Karting is where it all started for me and it taught me everything I’ve relied on throughout my career. “I know how hard it is for talented young drivers to get that first opportunity, especially when budgets are tight. “With the GR63 Karting Academy, I want to give something back by finding those hidden talents and giving them the support and platform they need to reach their potential. “I’m really grateful to Silverstone and the British Racing Drivers’ Club for helping make this happen.” George Russell has launched a new karting academy for drivers aged eight and nine David Coulthard, the former McLaren and Red Bull F1 driver who now serves as the president of the Silverstone-based British Racing Drivers’ Club (BRDC), added: “As owners of Silverstone and guardians of British motorsport, the BRDC has always been committed to reinvesting in the sport and nurturing home-grown talent. “That commitment has played a big part in Britain’s long record of success in motorsport and it is a great source of pride for the Club and its Members. “The GR63 Academy captures that ethos perfectly and we are delighted to work with George to support the next generation of drivers here at Silverstone.” More on George Russell and Mercedes from PlanetF1.com George Russell news Mercedes news The launch of Russell’s academy comes after Lando Norris, the McLaren driver and 2025 world champion, launched his own junior scheme in September. Norris set up the LN4 Legacy Programme to help unearth young motorsport talent, with the 26-year-old launching his own junior racing team called LN4 Fusion. It was confirmed last month that LN4 Fusion will compete in Formula 2 next season, with the team also having a presence in Formula 3, Formula Regional European Championship and Italian Formula 4. records.excerpt: FIA sets court hearing date in Audi F1 appeal against Yuki Tsunoda Oliver Harden 13 Nov 2026 11:24 AM Yuki Tsunoda could lose his 10th-place finish at Monza if Audi's appeal is successful The FIA has confirmed that an International Court of Appeal hearing into the Audi F1 team’s challenge against Yuki Tsunoda’s 10th-place finish at the Italian Grand Prix will take place in Paris on Wednesday November 25. The date will fall between the Las Vegas and Qatar grands prix. FIA sets date for Court of Appeal hearing into Audi F1’s Yuki Tsunoda challenge Tsunoda made three appearances for the Racing Bulls team after the summer break following an injury to Red Bull driver Isack Hadjar. The Japanese driver scored a single point on his return to action, finishing 10th at September’s Italian Grand Prix at Monza, where Audi F1 pair Gabriel Bortoleto and Nico Hulkenberg finished 11th and 12th respectively. Tsunoda had been due to start 14th, but initially went to line up in 15th on the opposite side of the grid. Realising his mistake, Tsunoda cut across the track at the last moment, leaving his car at an awkward angle and leading to FIA race director Rui Marques declaring an additional formation lap. Tsunoda went on to start the race from his original position and finished 10th, with Bortoleto and Hulkenberg crossing the line seven and eight seconds behind in 11th and 12th. Audi submitted an appeal against Tsunoda’s result three days after the race, after confirming it had “raised a concern regarding the application of Article B5.9.4” of the sporting regulations after Tsunoda went unpunished following an investigation into an alleged start procedure infringement. Article B5.9.4 reads: “Any driver who caused an extra formation lap, and is then able to start the, or any subsequent, extra formation lap must enter the Pit Lane at the end of the lap and must start the [session] from the end of the Pit Lane. “A Stop-and-Go Penalty will be imposed on any driver who fails to start the [session] from the Pit Lane.” Go deeper: What is the FIA? FIA explained: What does it stand for and how does it govern F1? Concorde Agreement explained: Who signs it, what it means and why it’s vital for F1 Tsunoda avoided a penalty on the day, with the FIA stewards opting to take no further action after accepting Racing Bulls’ explanation that Tsunoda did not explicitly cause an extra formation lap, with the decision for an additional formation lap taken by Marques. A section of the stewards’ verdict at Monza read: “The Race Director, in evidence, stated that it was his call, based on the behaviour of the car on the approach to the grid box, to commence an extra formation lap. He stated he was not comfortable starting the race with the car in that position.” Another section added: “The Stewards agree with the points [made by a Racing Bulls team representative] and consider that the extra formation lap resulted from the Race Director’s assessment of the situation, rather than being directly caused by the driver of Car 22.” The stewards also explained their decision to take no further action against Tsunoda, while recommending that the FIA establish a procedure to inform drivers and teams if they are specifically the cause of extra formation laps in the future. They wrote: “Article B5.9.4 goes on to specify that if a driver who causes the extra formation lap and is then able to start the extra formation lap, he must enter the Pit Lane at the end of the lap and start from the Pit Lane. “It is only then, if the driver fails to do this, that the mandatory penalty of a Stop and Go penalty is imposed. “In other words, the penalty is for failing to come into the Pit Lane and start from there. “The penalty is not for causing the extra formation lap, if indeed, he caused the extra formation lap in the first place. “A critical issue emerges here, in that in order to comply with the requirement to enter and start from the Pit Lane, a driver would need to know that he was the cause of the extra formation lap. “The team representative quoted situations where extra formation laps have been commenced due to extraneous circumstances such as the position of a photographer etc. “In this case, no message was sent to the team or the driver, advising them that they were the cause of the extra formation lap. “The team, based on the fact that the car was positioned within its starting grid box in compliance with the regulations, had, in our determination, no reason to instruct its driver to enter and start from the Pit Lane. “Accordingly, irrespective of whether or not the driver directly caused the extra formation lap, the team and driver were unaware that they were being considered as the cause, therefore we determine that we are unable to impose a Stop and Go penalty in this case, and decide to take no further action. “We note that the Race Director acted in good faith and out of an abundance of caution in ordering an extra formation lap. “We further note that the FIA might wish to consider implementing a process to advise teams and drivers if they are considered to be the cause of an extra formation lap, so that they are then able to comply with the requirements of Article B5.9.4.” Read next: Red Bull signs new reserve records.excerpt: Lawrence Stroll 'at wit's end' in new Brundle Aston Martin claim Lawrence Stroll ‘at wit’s end’ in new Brundle Aston Martin claim Jamie Woodhouse 13 Nov 2026 7:23 AM Aston Martin F1 team owner Lawrence Stroll Lawrence Stroll does not know where to turn next with the reliability woes for his Aston Martin team showing no signs of stopping. That is the claim made by Sky F1 commentator and pundit Martin Brundle, following recurring battery issues for Lance Stroll at the Brazilian Grand Prix. On a plus side for the team, Fernando Alonso displayed impressive pace in the changeable Interlagos conditions. Brundle: Lawrence Stroll ‘at wit’s end’ on reliability woes Lance, son of Aston Martin F1 team owner Lawrence Stroll, recorded his 14th DNF of the season at the Brazilian Grand Prix. “We were talking to Lawrence Stroll, the boss, about it. He’s at his wit’s end. He doesn’t know what to do about these endless reliability issues and non-finishes in the team,” Brundle claimed. “What are they going to do for next year? Have they got different ideas, different people to sort the problem out? The battery pack, the ERS, the energy recovery system and just the power deficit they’ve got. “That’s the problem Aston Martin have at the moment: Where do they go from here?” Following the Brazilian GP, Honda’s chief engineer Shintaro Orihara confirmed that investigations are ongoing into the battery issue which Stroll suffered twice at Interlagos. The root cause is “unknown” and it could take “a few weeks to find” it as the Japanese manufacturer conducts this deep dive. A key priority is to avoid any gremlins carrying over into F1 2027. More Aston Martin news on PlanetF1.com Adrian Newey compares Aston Martin trouble to Red Bull turmoil Adrian Newey weighs in on ‘two-tier’ F1 debate In terms of outright pace of the Aston Martin AMR26, that was very positive at Interlagos. Alonso booked his and the team’s first Q3 appearance of the season and drove on to a P12 result. That even included completing an overtake on former teammate Lewis Hamilton in the Ferrari. Aston Martin chief trackside officer Mike Krack highlighted this as a big upside, even if the team came away with no points. He also stressed that the issues with reliability need addressing, as is happening. “When the conditions were difficult, like yesterday, and also like today, I think the competitiveness was better, was improved, and especially today, I think it was a good performance,” he said post-race. “Considering the overall picture of the year, I think it was one of the most competitive yesterday and today. “Unfortunately, no points. That is what is always the takeaway of a weekend. “But I think all in all, we have beaten some competitors that are faster, that have certainly faster cars. So I think, yeah, a positive from that point of view. “But also, just if you review the last triple header or this triple header, we had five DNFs also out of six races. So that is something we certainly need to work on. “So a positive from the competitiveness, from that side, but not so positive on reliability.” Aston Martin sits 10th in the Constructors’ Championship standings with one triple-header remaining to bring F1 2026 to its conclusion. Williams is one position and five points up the road. records.title: Christian Horner reveals Adrian Newey demanded £6million a year to join Red Bull
records.excerpt: Christian Horner has recalled how Red Bull was stunned by Adrian Newey’s reported £6 million annual salary demand during negotiations to bring the celebrated Formula 1 designer from McLaren in 2005. In his memoir, Drive, Horner says Red Bull founder Dietrich Mateschitz initially reacted angrily when told the figure, calling it “obscene” and “disgusting”. He Christian Horner has recalled how Red Bull was stunned by Adrian Newey’s reported £6 million annual salary demand during negotiations to bring the celebrated Formula 1 designer from McLaren in 2005. In his memoir, Drive, Horner says Red Bull founder Dietrich Mateschitz initially reacted angrily when told the figure, calling it “obscene” and “disgusting”. He eventually changed his mind, however, and instructed Horner to complete the deal. Horner was leading Red Bull through its first season in Formula 1 when he began pursuing Newey, whose designs had helped Williams and McLaren win world championships. Newey joined Red Bull in 2006 and became a central figure in the team’s rise to the front of the sport. Horner writes that he first approached Newey after spotting him looking around Red Bull’s hospitality unit at the 2005 San Marino Grand Prix at Imola. With talk that Newey was unhappy at McLaren, Horner thought he might be open to a move. Horner discussed the possibility with David Coulthard, who had joined Red Bull from McLaren earlier that year. “Having Adrian at Red Bull would be a dream,” Horner recalled saying. Coulthard responded: “You’ll have to convince his wife, Marigold. She’s the key.” Horner describes Marigold Newey as “a formidable operator and an expert negotiator”. He continued trying to persuade the couple, including inviting them to the premiere of the latest Star Wars film after Red Bull’s partnership with the franchise. At a restaurant in Chelsea, Coulthard reportedly told Horner: “You focus on Adrian. I’ll deal with Marigold.” The negotiations advanced during a visit to Red Bull’s Hangar-7 facility in Austria, where Mateschitz hosted Horner, Coulthard and the Neweys. Horner says Marigold appeared anxious about being seen with her husband at Red Bull while he was still under contract to McLaren. He recalls that she brought a baseball cap and dark glasses for Newey, concerned that McLaren boss Ron Dennis might discover the visit. After dinner, Horner sensed that Newey was interested and asked him to join Red Bull as chief technical officer. Marigold replied that they would sign if the team matched Newey’s McLaren salary. Horner says he had been told by Coulthard that Newey earned about £3 million a year at McLaren, a sum Mateschitz was prepared to match. When Horner asked Marigold to confirm the figure, she reportedly said: “Six million pounds is his base salary. That’s what you would need to match.” Horner writes that he immediately left the table to call Mateschitz. He first told him that Newey was willing to join if Red Bull matched his salary, prompting an enthusiastic response. When Horner revealed the amount, Mateschitz erupted. “‘That’s obscene!’ he yelled. ‘No … It’s disgusting. How can one person earn so much money?’” Horner writes. Mateschitz told him to send Newey home, then ended the call. Horner says he was returning to the table without an offer when Mateschitz called again. Having calmed down, the Red Bull founder told him: “This is the right thing for the team. Go for it.” He then added: “Just make it happen.” The main points of the agreement were settled with a handshake, Horner says, although one detail remained: Newey wanted to take his drawing board from McLaren’s factory. He had also used it at Williams and insisted it should follow him to Red Bull. Horner recalls telling him: “You know Ron’s going to kill me when I ask him, don’t you?” Horner says Dennis gave him an “explosive dressing-down” over the request. Red Bull offered to make a donation to a charity chosen by Dennis to help resolve the matter. Newey’s work proved instrumental in Red Bull’s championship success. During Horner’s 20-year leadership of the team, Red Bull won six constructors’ championships and eight drivers’ titles, shared equally between Sebastian Vettel and Max Verstappen. Newey left Red Bull in 2024 and began work at Aston Martin in March 2025 as managing technical partner, becoming a shareholder in the team. He was subsequently promoted to team principal ahead of the 2026 season. Aston Martin has also disclosed that Newey holds an estimated 4.7 per cent stake in its Formula 1 team through an alphabet shareholding.

records.title: 「チーム版ADUO」はF1の格差を埋めるか、“コストキャップの罠”に挑む改革案が16日協議へ
records.excerpt: Courtesy Of Williams 「チーム版ADUO」はF1の格差を埋めるか、“コストキャップの罠”に挑む改革案が16日協議へ 公開： 2026/11/15 02:45 F1の下位チームに追加支出を認める「チーム版ADUO」が、11月16日（月）のF1コミッションで協議される見通しとなった。イギリスのモータースポーツ専門メディア『The Race』によると、ウィリアムズのチーム代表ジェームズ・ヴァウルズが訴えてきた提案が、正式に議題に挙げられるという。 これは、チャンピオンシップの得点または順位に連動して下位チームに追加支出を認める案だ。現時点で2027年の導入に必要な支持を確保するのは難しい情勢だが、上位チームからも人材確保のために給与面の制約を緩めるよう求める声が上がっており、コストキャップの見直しを巡る議論が活発化している。 「コストキャップの罠」ヴァウルズが訴える格差の固定化 ヴァウルズはこれまで、コストキャップが各チームの財務状況を安定させた点を評価する一方、小規模チームにとっては大規模な設備投資の阻害要因になっていると主張してきた。 最近のF1では、メルセデス、フェラーリ、マクラーレン、レッドブルという、いわゆる「ビッグ4」が支配的な競争力を誇っている。この4チームはコストキャップ導入以前に、設備や開発環境へ多額の資金を投じてきた。一方、ウィリアムズを含む小規模チームはそうではなかった。 そのため、ある意味で コストキャップはトップ4チームの優位性を固定化している というのが、ヴァウルズの問題提起だ。 ウィリアムズでは、ファクトリー内で部品の所在を管理する基本的なシステムすら整っておらず、マシン開発に充てる予算との配分が課題になっているという。ヴァウルズは、長年の投資不足を現在の支出制限の中で補わなければならない状況を「コストキャップの罠」と表現している。 ADUOという名称は、パワーユニット（PU）メーカー向けの追加開発・アップグレード機会制度（ADUO）に由来する。 この制度では、内燃エンジン（ICE）の性能で基準となるメーカーに一定以上の差をつけられた場合、追加の改良機会や予算、ベンチ試験時間の優遇が認められる。一方「チーム版ADUO」では、選手権順位や獲得ポイントに応じて追加支出を認める仕組みが検討されている。 「一夜にして実現しない」制度導入へ長期戦を覚悟 2027年からの規則変更には、国際自動車連盟（FIA）とF1の商業権を管理するフォーミュラ・ワン・マネジメント（FOM）に加え、全11チーム中6チームの支持が必要となる。現時点で賛同しているのは、キャデラック、アルピーヌ、アストンマーティン・ホンダ、アウディ、ウィリアムズの5チームにとどまると考えられている。 ビッグ4以外の2チームのうちハースは、現在の予算がコストキャップの上限を下回っており、今回の案によるメリットがないため反対しているという。一方、レーシング・ブルズも、 チーム代表アラン・パーメインが提案を支持しない考えを示している 。 このように、現状では2027年からの変更に1票足りない状況だが、2028年からの変更であれば、必要なチーム票は4つに減る。FIAとFOMの支持も必要だが、ヴァウルズは両組織が変更を「支持している」と説明している。 次の技術レギュレーションの変更は2030年または2031年が想定されている。ヴァウルズは次のように語り、それまでにチーム版ADUOを実現させたいとの考えを示している。 「一夜にして実現するとは思っていない。以前にも話したように、私が確実にしたいのは、次のレギュレーション変更までに適切な制度を整えることだ。それまではもう少し時間があるので、検討する余裕はある」 下位は設備投資、上位は人件費…改革に妥協の余地 上位チームも、現行のコストキャップに満足しているわけではない。人件費を抑制しなければならず、その結果、求職者に好条件を提示するテクノロジー企業などとの人材獲得競争で不利になり、優秀なエンジニアを引き留めることが難しくなっている。 こうした状況を受け、コストキャップの対象外として認められる人件費の枠を拡大する案が支持を集めつつあるとされる。現行の財務規則では、リザーブドライバーやテストドライバーを含むドライバーと、チーム内で最も高額な報酬を受け取る上位3人の費用がコストキャップの算定対象から外されている。 設備投資の余地を広げたいウィリアムズら下位チームと、人材確保のために給与面の制約を緩めたい上位チーム。双方が現行制度に変更を求めていることから、支出の対象や条件面の調整を通して、妥協点が見出される余地はありそうだ。 TAG： おすすめ レギュレーション/ルール F1 googlePreferred Google優先ソースに追加 installDesktop ホーム画面に追加 records.title: FIA、ADUOの追加改良枠は変更なし 2027年に向け制度改善を検討／F1（TopNews）
records.excerpt: FIA、ADUOの追加改良枠は変更なし 2027年に向け制度改善を検討／F1 11/13(金) 5:02 配信 2026年、F1サンパウロGP(C)Red Bull Content Pool（TopNews） ■最終審査でも新たな改良枠の付与なし FIA（国際自動車連盟）は、ADUO制度に基づき、2026年と2027年にパワーユニット（PU）メーカーに認める追加の改良枠に変更はないと発表した。一方、論争を呼んでいる同制度には改善の余地があると認めた。 ●【F1ライブ結果速報】F1サンパウロGP予選・決勝も全セッションライブでお届け 今季3回目で最後となるADUO審査では、新たな改良枠は付与されず、レッドブル・フォードの内燃エンジンが引き続き性能評価の基準となった。 この制度により、2026年と2027年の各年に、メルセデスは1回、フェラーリ、アウディ、ホンダは2回ずつ、改良したエンジンの追加公認を受けられる。 メルセデスがドライバーズ、コンストラクターズの両選手権を席巻する一方、制度上の評価基準ではレッドブル・フォードの内燃エンジンが最も高性能と判定されていることが、論争を招いている。 FIAは「最も性能の高い内燃エンジンに対する相対的な性能差には変化がありましたが、その変化によって新たな公認枠が付与されるには至りませんでした」と説明した。 ■トンバジス、制度の継続的な改善に言及 FIAシングルシーター技術部門責任者のニコラス・トンバジスは、審査結果の妥当性を主張しつつ、制度には改善の余地があると認めた。 「導入初年度の運用を通じて、ADUOの考え方がF1にとって適切だという私たちの確信は、さらに強まりました。ただし、この制度が効率的で、実情に即し、目的に適したものであり続けるよう、今後も改善を重ねていくことが重要です」 この発表に先立ち、フェラーリF1のフレデリック・バスール代表は、エンジン性能で後れを取っていることに、特にもどかしさを感じていると明かしていた。 「シャシーの性能で多少後れを取っていても、翌週のアップグレードで挽回できるという期待は常に持てます。しかし、エンジンの性能で多少後れを取っている場合は、シーズンの残りもその状態が続くと分かっています」 次回のADUO審査は、2027年の開幕から6戦を対象に行われる。 【関連リンク】 ●ロシアGP元主催者、F1の支払い要求に反論「開催されていない」 ●バスール代表「良い仕事をした」雨用タイヤに相次いだ批判もピレリを擁護／フェラーリF1 ●ホンダF1、信頼性後退を認める 直近3戦で5度のリタイア「根本原因は分かっていません」 ●ペレス、総額160億円の契約延長報道を否定せず レッドブル時代超えか／キャデラックF1 ●「F1史上最も競争の激しい時代」へ 両タイトル獲得のメルセデス代表、来季の王座争いに危機感／サンパウロGP

records.title: トト・ヴォルフ F1コストキャップの給与制限に異議「若手スタッフの待遇改善を」
records.excerpt: メルセデスF1のチーム代表トト・ヴォルフが、F1のコストキャップ制度によって若手スタッフの給与が抑制されているとして、FIA（国際自動車連盟）に特例措置を提案していたことを明かした。 2021年に導入されたコストキャップは、チーム間の支出格… トト・ヴォルフ F1コストキャップの給与制限に異議「若手スタッフの待遇改善を」 2026年11月14日 14:28 公開 メルセデスF1のチーム代表トト・ヴォルフが、F1のコストキャップ制度によって若手スタッフの給与が抑制されているとして、FIA（国際自動車連盟）に特例措置を提案していたことを明かした。 2021年に導入されたコストキャップは、チーム間の支出格差を縮小することを目的としている。しかし、近年は開発や設備投資への制約が問題視されており、ヴォルフは競争力とは直接関係しない従業員の待遇にも影響が及んでいると指摘した。 メルセデスF1がFIAに提案した若手スタッフの給与特例 F1のコストキャップをめぐっては、ウィリアムズのチーム代表ジェイムス・ボウルズが制度の見直しを求めている。特に設備投資に対する制約が、チーム間の格差を縮めるという本来の目的とは逆の結果を生み出しているとの懸念を示してきた。 ブラジルGPでは、コストキャップによる予算上の制約が各チームの部品運用を限界まで追い込み、パワーユニット交換によるグリッド降格が相次ぐ一因になっているのではないかとの見方について、ヴォルフが質問を受けた。 「コストキャップが導入された理由は理解している。しかし、我々はあらゆる面で限界ぎりぎりのところにいる。もう少し余裕があった方がいいのは確かだ」 「我々の場合、古いシャシーを来年に持ち越すことができない。何台かは切断して処分しなければならない。これらのマシンが残してきた記録を考えると、非常に残念なことだ」 「だから、どのチームもプレッシャーを受けている。条件は同じだ。私としては、予算の上限がもう少し引き上げられていればよかったと思う」 その一方で、メルセデスはコストキャップの見直しについて、マシン開発とは異なる観点から独自の提案を行っていたという。 「我々が考えていたのは、チームに加入した若手スタッフに対して、より良い給与を支払えるようにするための追加枠を設けることだった。入社して最初の5年、6年、7年の間、給与が抑えられてしまうような状況を避けたかった」 「そこで我々はFIAに提案した。フロントウイングをさらに開発するための予算ではなく、給与を少し引き上げるための追加枠を認めてほしいというものだ。コストキャップが、そうした部分まで抑え込んでしまっているからだ」 「しかし、当然ながら、この提案はあまり好意的には受け止められなかったよ（笑）」 ヴォルフの説明によれば、メルセデスが求めたのは開発費の増額ではなく、若手スタッフの待遇改善を目的とした給与面の特例だった。ただし、FIAから十分な支持を得ることはできなかったという。 コストキャップ見直しをめぐりF1チーム代表の議論が拡大 コストキャップのあり方については、アストンマーティンF1のチーム代表エイドリアン・ニューウェイも、競争力に応じた予算配分という考え方に言及している。 ニューウェイは、風洞実験の時間配分やパワーユニット開発におけるADUO（追加開発・アップグレード機会）の仕組みを例に挙げ、競争力で後れを取るチームに追加の開発機会を認める制度がすでに存在すると指摘した。 「風洞実験や、エンジンに関するADUOのような仕組みを見れば、後方にいるチームには、上位にいるチームよりも多くの風洞実験時間やダイナモテストの時間などが認められている」 「そう考えれば、その仕組みを予算にも広げることは容易に想像できる。つまり、後れを取っているチームには、予算面でも少し追加の余裕を与えるということだ」 ニューウェイが競争力に応じた予算配分の可能性に言及する一方、ヴォルフの提案は、チーム内で働く若手人材の給与に焦点を当てたものだった。 メルセデスは2026年、キミ・アントネッリのドライバーズタイトルとコンストラクターズタイトルを獲得し、2021年以来となる両選手権制覇を達成した。 その王座奪還を果たしたチームの代表が、コストキャップによる制約のなかでも、若手スタッフの待遇改善を優先課題のひとつとしてFIAに提案していたことが明らかになった。 この記事の画像を見る（全2枚） SHARE ポスト シェア LINE B! ブックマーク Pocket

records.title: 'ADUO for teams' plan to be discussed by F1
records.excerpt: Sweeping changes to cost cap rules look set to become a key area of discussion on Monday when an “ADUO for teams” proposal is debated at the Formula 1 Commission Formula 1 'ADUO for teams' plan to be discussed by F1 Jon Noble 14 Nov 2026 — 4 min read Sweeping changes to cost cap rules look set to become a key area of discussion on Monday when an “ADUO for teams” proposal is debated at the Formula 1 Commission. As first revealed by The Race, Williams team boss James Vowles has tabled the idea of a spending catch-up mechanism to help F1 teams escape what he thinks has become a “cost cap trap”. Vowles argues that while the cost cap has done a great job making all teams financially viable, it has also locked in legacy advantages that make it difficult for smaller teams to catch up with the bigger squads. He is pushing for a sliding scale catch-up system within the cost cap that allows the teams outside of the top four to spend more. It would mean those teams that finish bottom of the standings get greater financial freedom to help them close the gap to squads at the front. Vowles’ proposal has been added to the agenda of next week’s F1 Commission meeting, with it becoming formally known as “ADUO for teams”. This is in reference to the ADUO (Additional Development and Upgrade Opportunities) that exists for engine manufacturers - who are given extra spending allowances, dyno hours and homologation opportunities if their power unit is adrift of the benchmark. Vowles had originally hoped to get enough backing for the plan for it to get voted through the F1 Commission and into the rulebook as early as next year. For that to happen, it would have required support from the FIA, FOM plus six of the current 11 teams for what is known as a supermajority. But backing from five others appears unlikely, with only Cadillac, Alpine, Aston Martin and Audi supportive so far. Haas is against because it is not near the current cost cap limit so is not limited on spending, while Racing Bulls team boss Alan Permane has said he does not back the concept. The divided opinion in the paddock does not mean that the idea is dead, though, as support from four teams in total would be enough to get it into play for 2028. That would be early enough for it to then help shape things for the next rules era that is due to start in 2030 or 2031. Vowles said recently that a compromise solution remained possible - especially with support from the FIA and F1 over his plans - but implementation may not be swift. “What's more important to me, perhaps, is I have the support of the FIA and Formula 1 behind it,” he said. “I don't think we have an accurate enough direction that we need to take it in, that is right for the sport, which is still being discussed behind the scenes. “What I can say is the support is there. “I don't think it's going to happen overnight. As I previously mentioned, what I want to make sure is that we get it right by the next regulation change, which is a little way off, so we have some time. “But my suspicion on it is you'll see more and more being discussed over the next few months in that regard.” But Vowles’ idea is not the only cost cap change that is under the spotlight, because these discussions look set to trigger arguments about wider reform. Parts versus people F1’s top teams have little to gain from the idea of an “ADUO for teams”, as the biggest beneficiaries would be those squads hoping to close them down. But that does not mean the big squads are satisfied with how the current cost cap rules work, as they too are seeking changes to the regulations - to help F1 stay competitive. One of the hottest topics among them is the way that current cost cap limits are impacting the retention of staff and the ability of F1 as a whole to keep hold of the brightest engineers. Teams operating under the cost cap are forced to keep a lid on salaries, and that has left many F1 teams fighting a losing battle to retain talented personnel who are getting lured away by big-money offers from tech companies. There are also many stories of staff being able to earn better money in other racing series outside of F1 because the cost cap has put a ceiling on wages so much. The issue has increased in importance amid a global cost-of-living crisis, with F1’s cost cap increase tightly linked to inflation so teams are unable to lift salaries to respond to what staff need. A strong argument that is now gathering some pace is for the cost cap to evolve and separate spending on parts and spending on people. As has long been the case with F1’s rules, only the three highest-paid personnel within an organisation are exempt from being included within the cost cap. There were discussions in the past about expanding this to include up to 300 staff, but it is thought that this would be too wide a net and would effectively make the cost cap ineffective. Speaking at the Brazilian Grand Prix last weekend, Mercedes boss Toto Wolff said that his squad had long proposed a mitigating mechanism - but this was shot down. He told Sky F1: “I would have loved to have a little bit of an uplift. The idea that we had was that with more junior personnel that joined the team, we would have more allowance to pay them better and not [having] the salaries suppressed in the first five, six, seven years. “So we've pitched that to the FIA to give us an allowance, not for more front wings but an allowance for salaries to come up a little bit because the cost cap suppresses all of that. But obviously that didn't score a lot of brownie points.” Advertisement 00:00

records.title: F1 journalist receives FIA ban in Ferrari dispute as boycott announced
records.excerpt: F1 journalist receives FIA ban in Ferrari dispute as boycott announced Jamie Woodhouse 14 Nov 2026 9:15 AM The FIA is Formula 1's governing body Veteran Formula 1 journalist Jonathan McEvoy states that he has banned from the Formula 1 paddock for the final triple-header which brings F1 2026 to an end. This has led to his publication, the Daily Mail, announcing that it will boycott Formula 1 in response to what it calls a ‘draconian’ ban. Former F1 supremo Bernie Ecclestone has weighed in on the situation. Formula 1 journalist receives FIA paddock ban McEvoy noted that his accreditation has been revoked for the remainder of the season, to be restarted from the start of 2027. He has pointed the finger at Ferrari for this development, following a comment about Charles Leclerc in a column which he wrote, published between the Mexican and Brazilian GPs. Leclerc had drawn the ire of teammate Lewis Hamilton after a first-lap incident between the Ferraris in Mexico City, a spat which the Brit carried over into Interlagos before a pivotal sit-down discussion which squashed the beef. In a statement, an FIA spokesperson said: “As set out in the 2026 FIA Formula One World Championship Guidelines, media accreditation is granted at the sole discretion of the FIA and may be revoked at any time without notice. The Guidelines state that the highest standards of fairness and professionalism are expected as a minimum requirement for media accreditation.” The decision has sparked debate online among fellow journalists and fans. It has now been confirmed by the Daily Mail that in response to McEvoy’s ban, the publication will not report on races or press conferences across the final three rounds of F1 2026 in Las Vegas, Qatar and Abu Dhabi. “This is an unprecedented and outrageous attack on the freedom of the press,” said the Daily Mail’s head of sport Chris Dean regarding McEvoy’s ban. “We are in dangerous territory when the FIA react in such a heavy-handed way to some mild and fair criticism of one driver. “Jonathan McEvoy is a fearless and first-rate journalist who takes readers behind the curtain of F1’s shiny exterior. The FIA should reinstate his accreditation immediately.” In a statement to the publication, former F1 chief Bernie Ecclestone expressed his shock over the McEvoy development. “I don’t know why the FIA would ever do that,” the 96-year-old said. “Apart from the fact I like Jon, he is doing a fantastic job. “I look forward to reading what he’s writing. I don’t have to, it’s my choice to do that. I think it’s completely mad.” Latest Formula 1 news on PlanetF1.com ‘That’s obscene’ – Adrian Newey Red Bull salary demand revealed in Horner book claim ‘Something not right’ at Ferrari in telling Felipe Massa verdict F1 2026 resumes next week with the Las Vegas Grand Prix. From there, the sport returns to the Middle East for the Qatar and Abu Dhabi Grands Prix, as the season comes to a close. While Mercedes has secured the F1 2026 title double, second in the Drivers’ Championship remains up for grabs as George Russell bids to secure the Mercedes clean sweep. His deficit to Max Verstappen, currently occupying that P2 slot, is 17 points. Read next: ‘How wrong I was’ – How Michael Schumacher took Mercedes insider by surprise FIA

records.title: FIA penalty decision under Audi microscope after Brazilian GP
records.excerpt: FIA penalty decision under Audi microscope after Brazilian GP Jamie Woodhouse 14 Nov 2026 12:43 PM Nico Hulkenberg driving the Audi R26 Audi racing director Allan McNish stated that the incident which triggered a Nico Hulkenberg 10-second penalty in Brazil was a “very debatable situation” to the team. Hulkenberg was adjudged to have left the track and gained an advantage versus Franco Colapinto during the race. It was not clear to Audi which driver had the corner, while the fact that its driver had pulled away from Colapinto after overtaking also complicated the response. Audi explains why Nico Hulkenberg did not yield position Hulkenberg had emerged from his pit-stop behind the Alpine racer. “When we did the pit-stop, coming out, Colapinto was at the end of his stint on old tyres, hanging on, and ran him wide into Turn 1,” McNish stated after the race. “Did it again because Nico was on the outside, just pushed him wide, missed the apex. But because Nico went off and then was deemed to have gained the long and lasting advantage, then we had a 10-second penalty.” The Scott was asked why Audi did not instruct Hulkenberg to give the place back, considering the penalty threat which comes with completing an overtake off-track. He had scuttled across the T1/2 run-off and rejoined ahead of the Argentine. “Because for us it wasn’t clear,” McNish argued. “Normally, if you’re ahead at the apex, then you have the right to be given position. “Where the apex of Turn 1 is, because of how it drops down into the esses, it’s very subjective where the apex is. “Now, Colopinto never hit the apex. He was nowhere near the apex. He was a long way from the apex. But the FIA defined where the apex line was, and at that point, Colopinto ran wide out. “So for us, it was a very debatable situation, and we honestly didn’t know which way to go with it. If we had given it back, then we were stuck into the same position. “And the other factor was that by the time we had been able to review, Nico was gone so far ahead. He pulled two seconds on a lap, or 1.8 seconds. “So it’s one that always you have to follow the FIA ruling. There’s no question. But it wasn’t clear for us that it wasn’t Nico’s corner.” Latest Audi news on PlanetF1.com FIA sets court hearing date in Audi F1 appeal against Yuki Tsunoda Audi lands major signing in ex-Mercedes F1 engine chief Hulkenberg’s response to the penalty was declared a “statement” by his team’s racing director. He recovered to bag the final point on offer in 10th. “But when it turned into the intermediate, he had pushed ahead, pulled ahead from Arvid Lindblad, and then in the intermediate, he was on a mission,” McNish continued. “Straight onto the back of Lindblad, and the overtake was one that definitely I think was good, aggressive, and it was also a delivery of that’s a statement. ‘Yeah, give us a penalty, but we can still get it back.'” Read next: ‘How wrong I was’ – How Michael Schumacher took Mercedes insider by surprise Audi FIA Franco Colapinto Nico Hulkenberg

records.title: F1 Academy News: Champion Alisha Palmowski Joins Red Bull Junior Team
records.excerpt: Title: F1 Academy News: Champion Alisha Palmowski Joins Red Bull Junior Team URL Source: http://www.autoracing1.com/pl/509441/f1-academy-news-champion-alisha-palmowski-joins-red-bull-junior-team/ Final URL: https://www.autoracing1.com/pl/509441/f1-academy-news-champion-alisha-palmowski-joins-red-bull-junior-team/ Published Time: 2026-11-13T09:59:26+00:00 Markdown Content: Newly crowned F1 Academy champion, Alisha Palmowski (pictured) joins the illustrious Red Bull Junior program from 2027 as Red Bull commits to supporting her future. After two years with the Red Bull Racing Academy program in the all-female racing series, F1 ACADEMY, Alisha embarks on the next steps of her career having won the F1 ACADEMY title in Austin. As part of the Red Bull Junior Team, Alisha will make the step up to Formula Regional European Championship (FREC), where she will race for Rodin Motorsport in the 2027 season while receiving the support and development of the Red Bull Junior program. Red Bull is dedicated to providing a proven pathway for future motorsport talents, and Alisha’s graduation from [F1 ACADEMY](https://www.f1academy.com/) to the Red Bull Junior program is a demonstration of that commitment. As she begins the next chapter of her career, Alisha will receive the continued support and development of the Red Bull Junior program. Alisha will conclude her time with the Red Bull Racing Academy program in F1 ACADEMY next weekend in Las Vegas where she heads into the final round with 172 points and a 53-point lead at the top of the standings. **Laurent Mekies, CEO and Team Principal of Oracle Red Bull Racing, said:** “We are very happy to keep Alisha in the Red Bull family and continue this journey together! Over the past two seasons, she has developed exceptionally well, both on and off the track. She has consistently performed at a very high level despite the pressure of going into the season as the favorite, culminating in a dominant championship-winning campaign. We recognize the importance of F1 Academy in creating opportunities for young drivers to develop and showcase their talent, and at Red Bull we have always taken that responsibility very seriously. As Alisha continues her development in the Red Bull Junior Team, we can’t wait to support her as she competes against other very talented young men and women in FRECA next year.” **Alisha Palmowski, F1 Academy Champion and Red Bull Racing Academy program driver, said:** “I’m so excited to continue my journey with Red Bull. I joined this family just under two years ago as a young girl with dreams of making them come true. Winning the title in Austin, with my family there and so many people from Red Bull, was surreal, and it’s a weekend I’ll never forget. I’ve developed so much as a driver and as a person over the last two seasons, and the support I’ve received from Campos Racing, Red Bull and F1 ACADEMY has been incredible. It’s taken a lot of hard work to get here, and I know there’s still a lot more to do, but having Red Bull’s belief behind me makes the journey clearer. Next season brings a new series, a new team and a fresh opportunity to test myself. Moving up the single-seater ladder has always been the goal, and I’m incredibly grateful to have the opportunity to race in Formula Regional with Rodin Motorsport. I can’t wait to get going.” Having shown true progress and ability throughout her motorsport journey, Red Bull has committed to Alisha’s future beyond F1 ACADEMY and in joining the Red Bull Junior program, she is following the path taken by Max Verstappen, Sebastian Vettel, Daniel Ricciardo and Isack Hadjar.

records.label: motorsport.com
records.title: James Allison admits flawed “Update 18” made the Mercedes W17 a “handful”
records.excerpt: James Allison admits Mercedes' late-season "Update 18" upgrade introduced unexpected flaws that made the W17 a handful Mercedes stormed out of the gates in 2026, quickly establishing a dominant lead that ultimately secured both the drivers' and constructors' championships. But as the season nears its conclusion, the performance gap between the W17 and the rest of the grid has visibly shrunk. According to Mercedes technical director James Allison, this convergence was not just a natural result of rivals catching up. Speaking on the NU Silver Arrows Radio Show, Allison confessed that Mercedes' own development path actively hampered the car's driveability late in the year. While discussing the shrinking gap to the competition, Allison pointed to the team's latest major aerodynamic package. George Russell, Mercedes, Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes Photo by: Colin McMaster / LAT Images via Getty Images "Our final step of performance, our so-called 'Update 18', the thing we brought to the Sepang track and then followed up with the front wing in America... it has given us more downforce, but it has made the car more of a handful," Allison admitted. Rather than delivering a pure step forward in-lap time, the new parts introduced unpredictable side effects. "It's got some areas where it has subtracted a bit of performance that we were not expecting," Allison explained. The "skinny" weight advantage Allison's admission regarding 'Update 18' also shed light on why the W17 looked so untouchable during the opening rounds of the championship. For the 2026 regulations, the FIA mandated a sweeping 30-kilogram weight reduction across the grid, dropping the minimum chassis weight to just 768 kilograms. While other constructors struggled to shed the mass, Mercedes nailed the engineering target immediately. Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes Photo by: Clive Rose / Formula 1 via Getty Images "We were also probably the only car on the weight limit at the start of the year," Allison revealed. "All the folk we were competing with in the championship had a bit of timber to shift, and that was lap time that came to them that wasn't available to us because we were already skinny and on the limit with the weight." As rival teams eventually lost their excess weight as the season progressed, the field naturally compressed – an effect exacerbated by Mercedes' flawed 'Update 18', making the W17 significantly harder to extract pace from.

records.title: Antonelli presents Italian president with signed helmet after F1 title
records.excerpt: Formula 1 world champion Andrea Kimi Antonelli visited President Sergio Mattarella at Rome's Quirinal Palace with his family, presented a signed Mercedes helmet and invited the Italian head of state to attend the 2027 Italian Grand Prix. News Summary Andrea Kimi Antonelli met Italian President Sergio Mattarella in Rome on November 13 following his historic 2026 Formula 1 championship victory. The Mercedes driver presented Mattarella with a signed helmet and invited him to attend the Italian Grand Prix at Monza in 2027. Mattarella said Antonelli’s championship success had renewed his interest in attending a Formula 1 race. Andrea Kimi Antonelli was received by Italian President Sergio Mattarella at the Quirinal Palace in Rome on Friday, November 13, following his historic Formula 1 world championship victory. The Mercedes driver, accompanied by his family, presented the head of state with a signed racing helmet and invited him to attend the Italian Grand Prix at Monza in 2027. The meeting marked another celebration of Antonelli’s achievement after he became Italy’s first Formula 1 world champion in 73 years. The 20-year-old secured the 2026 championship at the Mexico City Grand Prix, becoming the youngest drivers’ world champion in Formula 1 history. Andrea Kimi Antonelli and Sergio Mattarella, Italy’s president (Photo: Presidenza della Repubblica Italiana) Antonelli presents Mattarella with signed Mercedes helmet Antonelli attended the meeting with his father Marco, mother Veronica and sister Maggie. The Italian Presidency confirmed the private audience in an official statement, while photographs and video released by the Quirinal Palace showed the Mercedes driver presenting his helmet to Mattarella. The visor carried a handwritten dedication: “To President Mattarella, with great admiration.” The president examined the helmet and commented on how uncomfortable it must be to wear during a Grand Prix. Antonelli explained that drivers can lose approximately 2 kg during a race because of the heat inside the cockpit and the protective equipment required. “We lose a couple of kilos during a race, also because of the fireproof suit,” Antonelli explained, according to Sky Sport Italia . The Mercedes driver added that competitors train extensively to withstand the physical demands of Formula 1 and often use cold-water baths after particularly hot sessions. The conversation also touched on the differences between karting and single-seater racing, with Antonelli explaining that drivers are more exposed to airflow in karts than inside a Formula 1 cockpit. Antonelli invites Italian president to 2027 Monza Grand Prix The most significant exchange came when Antonelli invited Mattarella to attend the Italian Grand Prix. “You must come to Monza. It would be wonderful,” the Mercedes driver told the president. Mattarella responded positively, although he acknowledged that official travel arrangements could make attending difficult. “My movements have been rather complicated for several years, but this new situation really encourages me,” Mattarella said. The president was referring to the renewed excitement surrounding Formula 1 in Italy following Antonelli’s championship victory. Mattarella has attended the Italian Grand Prix in the past, but his presence at the 2027 race has not been confirmed. The invitation nevertheless illustrates the national significance of Antonelli’s achievement. Italy had not celebrated a Formula 1 drivers’ world champion since Alberto Ascari won his second consecutive title with Ferrari in 1953. Giuseppe Farina, the inaugural Formula 1 world champion in 1950, remains the country’s other title winner. Italy celebrates first F1 champion in 73 years Antonelli’s visit to the Quirinal Palace followed several public appearances and official honours. On November 12, he received the title of Commander of the Equestrian Order of Saint Agatha in San Marino, where he lives with his family. The decoration is one of the republic’s highest honours and recognised Antonelli’s sporting achievements and his connection with the country. Later that day, the Mercedes driver attended Italy’s football match against France at San Siro in Milan, where he received a standing ovation from supporters. The celebrations reflect the significance of a championship victory that ended a 73-year wait for Italy. Antonelli’s rapid rise has also increased expectations for the 2027 Formula 1 season, when he will attempt to defend his title against Max Verstappen, Lewis Hamilton, Charles Leclerc, Lando Norris and Mercedes teammate George Russell. As GRANDE PRÊMIO reported , Antonelli has identified Verstappen as his biggest individual threat for next year’s championship. The Red Bull driver has been the highest-scoring competitor over the latest five Grands Prix, highlighting how much closer the competition has become since Mercedes dominated the opening part of 2026. Antonelli returns to F1 action in Las Vegas Despite the celebrations, Antonelli still has three Grands Prix remaining in the 2026 season. Formula 1 returns to Las Vegas on November 19–21, followed by Qatar and Abu Dhabi. Mercedes has already secured both world championships, but the final races will provide further opportunities to assess the competitive balance ahead of 2027. Antonelli will arrive in Nevada as world champion for the first time, carrying the expectations of a country celebrating its first Formula 1 title since the early 1950s. The visit to Mattarella also underlined the wider significance of his success: Antonelli is no longer simply one of Italy’s leading racing drivers, but a national sporting figure whose achievements have reached the country’s highest political office. GRANDE PRÊMIO is following every session of the 2026 Formula 1 championship and preparations for the 2027 season.

records.excerpt: アステモ、新社長にホンダ四輪本部長の井上勝史氏 竹内弘平社長は退任 ホンダ四輪事業の立て直しを全面支援 – 日刊自動車新聞 2026.11.15(日) 管理者 紙面で読む 会社案内 各種申し込み 購読のご案内 ログイン 購読の ご案内 管理者 紙面で 読む ログイン 検索 トップ 自動車流通 開発・生産 行政・輸送 Home 自動車部品・素材・サプライヤー アステモ、新社長にホンダ四輪本部長の井上勝史氏 竹内弘平社長は退任 ホンダ四輪事業の立て直しを全面支援 自動車部品・素材・サプライヤー , 自動車メーカー , 人事・組織改正 2026年5月29日 11:30 SNSで共有: 井上勝史氏 ホンダと日立が出資する自動車部品メーカーのアステモ（東京都千代田区）は5月29日、ホンダの井上勝史取締役が7月1日付で社長CEO（最高経営責任者）に就任するトップ人事を内定したと発表した。竹内弘平社長CEOは退任する。6月25日の定時株主総会と7月1日の臨時取締役会を経て正式決定する。 井上氏はホンダの欧州や中国の責任者などを経て、電動事業開発部門のトップ、昨年4月には四輪事業本部長に就いたが、6月にホンダの取締役退任が決まっていた。 ホンダは日立が保有するアステモの株式21％分を取得し、出資比率を61％に引き上げて子会社化する予定でいる。電気自動車（EV）戦略の失敗で業績が悪化している同社は、ソフトウエア・デファインド・ビークル（SDV）やハイブリッド車（HV）に重点を置く方針に軌道修正した。アステモはSDVや電動車向けを含むパワートレイン技術に強い。ホンダはアステモの先進技術や開発力を高く評価しており、連携を強化する。 今回、ホンダの四輪事業部門で実務経験の長い井上氏にトップ交代することで、ホンダの四輪事業の立て直しについて、系列サプライヤーとして全面的に支える体制を整える。 竹内社長もホンダ出身で、2023年7月にアステモの社長に就いた。ホンダでは財務・管理部門が長く、アステモでは前任社長時代の品質問題を踏まえた対応や財務体質の改善、株式公開に向けた準備などを担ってきた。 井上勝史氏（いのうえ・かつし）1986年3月、横浜国立大学経営学部卒、同年4月ホンダ入社。2015年ホンダカーズインディア社長、16年ホンダ執行役員、欧州地域本部長、20年常務執行役員兼中国本部長兼本田技研工業（中国）投資総経理兼本田技研科技（中国）総経理、23年執行役専務兼電動事業開発本部長、25年取締役執行役専務兼四輪事業本部長兼リスクマネジメントオフィサー、25年6月同取締役執行役専務、26年4月同取締役。1963年10月22日生まれ、62歳。福岡県出身。 〈2026/5/29更新〉 SNSで共有: 関連記事 ホンダ、現実路線で四輪事業の収益改善へ 開発費・期間・工数を半減 「開発スピードは世界トップレベルに」 2026年5月15日 05:00 ｜ 自動車メーカー , 企画・解説・オピニオン ホンダ、電動化戦略を見直し EV目標は撤回 2029年度までに次世代HV15モデル投入 新型セダンとアキュラSUVも公開 2026年5月14日 14:10 ｜ 自動車メーカー ホンダ、アステモを子会社化 ソフトやAI開発加速 新規株式公開も視野 2025年12月18日 05:00 ｜ 自動車メーカー , 自動車部品・素材・サプライヤー ホンダ系サプライヤー、EV戦略見直しに「補償求める」「量産前の決断歓迎」などの声 2026年3月13日 05:00 ｜ 自動車部品・素材・サプライヤー 資本再編進む自動車サプライヤー 親子上場の解消 円安で外資も意欲 経営資源集中でEVやSDVに対応 2026年1月1日 05:00 ｜ 企画・解説・オピニオン , 自動車部品・素材・サプライヤー サーヴェンティスが2026～27年のカラートレンド予測、アジア太平洋は銀系の「ホライゾンフラックス」 2026年11月14日 05:00 ｜ 自動車部品・素材・サプライヤー アクセスランキング 直近 昨日 一週間 ワンソクTubeのブログはこちら 【レクサス大丈夫か?!】2026年上半期の新車販売台数ランキングTOP50で異変! 意外な車が上位へ?! レクサスを叱咤激励するオーナーたちの意外な本音とは?! records.title: エティハド航空、マクラーレン・レーシングの787特別塗装機を発表 ワイドボディ機へのF1塗装は初
records.excerpt: エティハド航空、マクラーレン・レーシングの787特別塗装機を発表 ワイドボディ機へのF1塗装は初 | sky-budget スカイバジェット コンテンツへスキップ sky-budget スカイバジェット お得で役立つ世界の航空情報をいち早く発信！ FSC 航空ニュース エティハド航空、マクラーレン・レーシングの787特別塗装機を発表 ワイドボディ機へのF1塗装は初 2026年11月13日 sky-budget編集部 エティハド航空は、パートナーであるマクラーレン・レーシングの象徴的なブランドデザインを施したボーイング787ドリームライナーの特別塗装機を発表しました。ワイドボディ機にF1チームのデザインが採用されるのは今回が初めてであり、モータースポーツと民間航空の歴史における新たな節目となります。 この特別塗装機は、世界的に認知されている両ブランドのパートナーシップを記念してデザインされたもので、エティハド航空の主力機である787に、マクラーレンを象徴する「パパイヤカラー」と独自のアイデンティティが大胆に描かれています。今後、本拠地のアブダビからダブリン、ミラノ、ウィーン、バリ、バンコク、デリーなど、エティハド航空の広範なグローバルネットワークを通じて世界各地へ運航され、世界中の乗客やファンとマクラーレン・レーシングをつなぐ役割を果たします。 機体のお披露目は、アブダビにあるエティハド・エンジニアリングの施設で行われました。この発表イベントでは、「世界最大の1枚布による振り落とし幕（カブキ・リビール）」の演出が実施され、ギネス世界記録に認定されるという華々しい形で幕を開けました。 エティハド航空のアントノアルド・ネベスCEOは、両社がパフォーマンスへのこだわりと常に前進し続ける情熱を共有する野心的なグローバルブランドであると述べた上で、「この航空機はその物語を私たちの本拠地であるアブダビから世界中の都市へと誇りを持って運び、飛行する先々でパートナーシップをファンの皆様のより身近なものにし、拡大するグローバルネットワークを通じてF1の興奮を共有していきます。F1には国境を越えて人々をつなぎ、熱狂を生み出す素晴らしい力があります。マクラーレンと共に、ファンをこれまで以上にアクションの近くへと導き、世界中で記憶に残る瞬間を創出できる機会を得ました。この機体が大空を舞う姿を見るのを心待ちにしています」と語りました。 今回の特別塗装機は、先に発表された2026年シーズンおよびそれ以降に向けた「マクラーレン・マスターカードF1チーム」ならびに「マクラーレン・ハイパーカー・チーム」のオフィシャルパートナー契約を象徴する最新の取り組みです。テクノロジー、チームワーク、そして高いパフォーマンスによって形作られる両業界の共通点を反映しており、マクラーレンが世界中でレースを戦う中、エティハド航空は日本、オーストラリア、中国、シンガポール、英国、スペイン、イタリア、アメリカといった主要なF1開催地とアブダビを結んでいます。Photo : Etihad Airways エティハド航空の躍進を支えたアリク・デ氏が退任 6月には来日し札幌・名古屋などの日本路線拡大に意欲 エティハド航空、約6年半の保管を経て最後のA380を路線復帰へ 間もなく9機体制 エティハド航空、新ブランド体験「Beyond Borders」とA330neoの新キャビンを発表 ファーストクラスを設定 Related posts: エティハド航空、2024年1月15日より東京/成田～アブダビ線にA350-1000型機を投入 エティハド航空幹部、今後発表する30の新路線にアジアの第2都市が含まれていることを示唆 スターラックス航空とエティハド航空がコードシェア契約を締結 エティハド航空の旅客は台北経由で日本各都市へ乗り継ぎ可能に エティハド航空幹部「イラン戦争後も成田線へのA380の投入見直しは全く検討しなかった。名古屋・札幌も就航検討に値する」

Secure .gov websites use HTTPS A lock ( ) or https:// means you’ve safely connected to the .gov website. Share sensitive information only on official, secure websites. United States Department of Transportation Commercial Space Transportation Countdown to launch. The FAA has reached a historic milestone with successful launch and reentry operations. See Stats Here FAA Reaches 1,000 Licensed Space Operations August 14, 2025 marked the FAA’s 1,000th operation of a commercial space vehicle that the agency licensed or permitted. The United States is a leader in space exploration, and this milestone highlights more than 35 years of the FAA successfully fulfilling its mission to protect safety and advance the future of our skies. The commercial space transportation industry emerged in the 1990s and was primarily used to launch commercial satellites and transport cargo to the International Space Station (ISS). In just the last few years, growing interest in commercial space is realizing new possibilities for the industry including providing transportation to the ISS laboratories for research and space tourism. This rapidly growing industry is inspiring scientists, engineers, teachers, and a whole generation, to imagine entirely new possibilities for the future of space. Safety Safety is our North Star. Compliance, Enforcement & Mishap Legislation & Policies Operations We protect the public, property, and U.S. national security interests. Airspace Integration Commercial Space Data Licensing We license all U.S. commercial launches and reentries here and abroad. Environmental Licenses, Permits and Approvals Stakeholder Engagement Vehicle Operator Licenses Industry Outreach We work collaboratively with industry to promote safety. Aerospace Rulemaking Committees: (SpARCs) COMSTAC Standards Development International We work with our international partners to promote safety. International Affairs Spaceports U.S. Spaceports are critical infrastructure for the industry. Office of Spaceports Spaceports by State Commercial Space By The Numbers Spaceports Map Find a U.S. spaceport near you. Map to commercial, government, and active private spaceports around the country. Learn about U.S. Spaceports Jobs What do we do? What careers are in commercial space? Commercial Space Transportation ensures that rocket launches and reentries are safe. We do this by applying a broad range of skillsets to manage licensing and regulatory work, as well as many programs and initiatives. Some examples of the jobs we do include inspecting reusable and expendable launch vehicles, assessing aerospace vehicle systems, developing public safety standards and requirements, assuring engineering quality, and assessing environmental impacts. Why does it matter? Our efforts help facilitate both the U.S. and global commercial space transportation industry’s health and growth. We value the talents, ideas, and insights that will enable us to continue our mission of ensuring and promoting the safest commercial space transportation in the world. Join us in exploring this exciting, meaningful, and innovative field! How can I find out more and apply? We are actively hiring qualified people to help us grow our team to meet the global commercial space community’s increasing demands. If you would like to find out more about being part of an organization where the possibilities are literally limitless, please take a look at Commercial Space Careers and email us at 9-AST-Comm-Space-Careers@faa.gov . records.title: SpaceX’s Starship returns from orbit and is captured by launchpad arms in a dramatic first
records.excerpt: CAPE CANAVERAL, Fla. — SpaceX’s Starship made a triumphant return to Earth on Saturday, caught in midair by giant mechanical arms where its journey began 22 hours earlier. CAPE CANAVERAL, Fla. — SpaceX’s Starship made a triumphant return to Earth on Saturday, caught in midair by giant mechanical arms where its journey began 22 hours earlier. It was the grand finale that Elon Musk and his team hoped for — the first-ever capture of a Starship flying back from space. But with the first-stage booster exploding shortly after Friday’s liftoff from Texas, the company fell short of its desired double catch, still the goal for accelerating moon and Mars travel. Wreckage remained in the Gulf of Mexico, cordoned off by buoys, as the stainless steel, bullet-shaped spacecraft lowered itself upright at the launch pad. The dramatic, sci-fi-like capture helped blot out the booster’s messy miss. Cameras panned the spacecraft up and down as it hung high above the ground, supported by the arms of the launch tower. “Can you believe it?” SpaceX commentator Dan Huot shouted, dragging out each word. “Look at her! Baby, she’s back!” Soon afterward, Musk congratulated his “incredible team.” SpaceX officials said Saturday’s catch demonstrates the full reusability of Starship, crucial for rapid and low-cost recycling. Although Friday’s booster recovery failed, the company had already made three previous booster catches, validating the technique. NASA welcomed Saturday’s news. The space agency is paying billions of dollars for Starship to land Artemis astronauts on the moon later this decade and help build a permanent lunar base. Musk’s ambitions are even grander: He wants to launch a fleet of Starships to build a city on Mars. “It was almost magic,” NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman said via X. “Making more believers by the day.” The world’s largest and most powerful rocket — a 407-foot (124-meter) behemoth — blasted off Friday afternoon from SpaceX’s Starship base near the U.S.-Mexican border. Separating neatly from its booster before things went awry, the upper-stage spacecraft soared into orbit and released 26 advanced Starlink satellites. Starship continued circling the world 165 miles up, with live views of itself and Earth streaming down via Starlink. The spacecraft completed 14 laps around Earth, outshining the previous mission’s one to two laps. It was SpaceX’s 15th flight of a full-scale Starship since 2023 and its only second trip to orbit. SpaceX reported that everything on the spacecraft, including its vital heat shield, appeared to work well. As for the booster, SpaceX’s Kate Tice said its engines stopped firing too soon on the way back down. The booster’s guidance system sensed it wasn’t in the right position and automatically initiated the watery detour and self-destruction. Engineers are still investigating the cause. SpaceX expects to begin launching Starships from Florida’s Kennedy Space Center within the next few months. That is the starting point for NASA’s next Artemis mission, which will skip the moon and remain in orbit around Earth for lunar lander practice. Artemis III’s four astronauts will attempt to dock their capsule with not only Starship but Blue Origin’s Blue Moon. The two companies will take turns delivering crews to the lunar surface. NASA is targeting as soon as 2028 for Artemis IV, humanity’s first moon landing since the Apollo era more than half a century ago.

records.title: SpaceX launches milestone Starship flight to demonstrate full reusability of orbit-class rocket
records.excerpt: SpaceX launches milestone Starship flight to demonstrate full reusability of orbit-class rocket - CBS News Watch CBS News Space SpaceX launches milestone Starship flight to demonstrate full reusability of orbit-class rocket By William Harwood CBS News Space Consultant Bill Harwood has been covering the U.S. space program full-time since 1984, first as Cape Canaveral bureau chief for United Press International and now as a consultant for CBS News. Read Full Bio William Harwood Updated on: November 13, 2026 / 9:10 PM EST / CBS News Add CBS News on Google SpaceX launched its huge Starship rocket on the program's 15th test flight Friday, a 22-hour mission that was meant to feature planned launch pad catches of both the booster and the Starship's upper stage. However, after the booster sent the Starship on its way to orbit as planned, a problem of some sort prevented a return-to-the-launch-pad capture. Instead, the rocket made a splashdown off the Texas Gulf Coast, exploding in a spectacular fireball moments before hitting the water. SpaceX managed to catch a Super Heavy booster during three previous test flights, using giant mechanical arms on the launch gantry to snag the rockets as they descended tail first on the power of three of their 33 Raptor engines. But the flight plans always include a splashdown option if an issue crops up preventing a safe capture. It was not immediately known what triggered the diversion Friday or the explosion before splashdown. SpaceX's Starship Flight 15 launches from Starbase in Boca Chica, Texas, on Nov. 13, 2026. Ricardo Arduengo/AFP via Getty Images It was a disappointment for SpaceX workers who had hoped the Super Heavy-Starship rocket's 15th test flight would be the first to demonstrate full reusability in an orbit-class rocket. The company still plans to attempt its first-ever launch pad catch of a Starship upper stage Saturday at the conclusion of the mission. Loaded with 8 million pounds of supercold liquid oxygen and methane fuel, the rocket's 236-foot-tall first stage, powered by 33 methane-burning Raptor engines, roared to life and majestically propelled the booster away from SpaceX's "Starbase" launch site on the Texas Gulf Coast at 5:47 p.m. ET. Arcing away to the southeast, the Super Heavy booster propelled the rocket out of the thick lower atmosphere before falling away about 2 minutes and 20 seconds after liftoff. Technical problem forced SpaceX to divert booster to Gulf Coast While the 171-foot-tall Starship continued the climb to space using six Raptors of its own, the booster flipped around and fired up a set of Raptors to reverse course and head back to the launch site. But a little more than 6 minutes after liftoff, flight controllers ordered a diversion to a Gulf Coast splashdown because of a technical problem. Long-range cameras captured the big booster slowly descending to the Gulf, shrouded in steam and then a fireball as residual propellants ignited. The Starship, meanwhile, followed a suborbital trajectory, ensuring a safe ocean splashdown in case of problems, while giving SpaceX flight controllers time to assess its health before committing to a final push to orbit. But no issues were found and after an 18-minute coast, a single Raptor reignited for a short 10-second burn to push the craft into its planned orbit. Eight and a half minutes after that, the first of 26 upgraded version 3 Starlink internet satellites was expected to be pushed out into space to fly on its own. For the rest of the flight, controllers planned to closely monitor the Starship, periodically assessing its health to make sure it could be safely de-orbited in case of problems that might prevent a safe return-to-launch-site capture at the same pad where it launched Friday atop the Super Heavy booster. It will be SpaceX's first attempt to get a Starship back to its pad for possible refurbishment and relaunch. "During this prolonged coast phase, flight control teams have several options to end the mission early and return Starship to pre-cleared areas of the Pacific Ocean if needed," SpaceX said in a blog post. "These locations include early- and late-mission splashdown options around Hawaii and a mid-mission splashdown opportunity several hundred kilometers off the coast of Chile. These precleared areas ... provide a safe place to land Starship if any conditions arise that may preclude the ability to perform a safe reentry." Starship's upper stage slated to reenter Earth's atmosphere and land at Starbase on Saturday One hour after a final "return check" Saturday, a single Raptor is expected to fire at 3:21 p.m. Eastern time to lower the far side of the Starship's orbit deep into the atmosphere for a 56-minute belly-first reentry and return to the Texas Gulf Coast. "During reentry, Starship can alter its flight path by moving its four control flaps," the company said. "This will permit Starship to maintain a safe and known trajectory while guiding itself with high precision control toward Starbase." As it descends, the Starship will carry out "a series of small turns in its trajectory to intentionally fly over sparsely populated areas of northern Mexico and southern Texas," SpaceX said. Starship will avoid major cities in the Rio Grande Valley and pass to the north of South Padre Island before heading "out over the Gulf of America as it makes its final turn south towards Starbase." Nearing the launch pad, the 171-foot-tall Starship will fire three Raptors to flip upright. Once the maneuver is complete, one Raptor will be shut down as the rocket descends between the gantry's mechanical arms. Finally, with just one engine firing to slow the rocket to a near stop, the mechanical arms will move in to snag the spacecraft. But all of that depends on a problem-free descent. If any problems develop that might lead to an uncontrolled landing, flight controllers can ensure a vehicle breakup before it has any chance to reach a populated area. "During reentry, flight controllers will have several options to end the reentry early and safely by intentionally tumbling Starship to ensure that it breaks up in the atmosphere before reaching land," SpaceX said. "There is also a late-reentry option to send Starship into the Gulf ... if any of its systems or the tower itself encounter an issue after reentry that would preclude a safe catch at Starbase." SpaceX calls development of a fully reusable rocket "the holy grail of rocketry," opening the door to airplanelike cadence where a vehicle flies again rapidly. NASA is counting on a variant of the Starship to carry Artemis astronauts to the lunar surface in 2028. But the rocket's development has taken longer than initially expected and the space agency is now hedging its bets, saying it is also open to using Blue Origin's Blue Moon Mark 2 lander depending on which spacecraft is ready. records.title: SpaceX Starship launch tests luck on Friday the 13th
records.excerpt: SpaceX Starship launch is set for Nov. 13. See what time, how to watch, the double catch plan and why ULA’s Vulcan slipped. SpaceX Starship launch tests luck on Friday the 13th The SpaceX Starship launch is only half the story, and the second half lands on Saturday By Gesi Lloyd Nov 13, 2026 2:30 pm Photo credit: Shutterstock.com / Wirestock Creators SpaceX is set to launch Starship on its 15th test flight today, Nov. 13, from Starbase in South Texas. The 75 minute launch window opens at a quarter to 6 p.m. ET. The goal is a first in rocket history: catching both the Super Heavy booster and the ship upper stage back at the launch tower. United Launch Alliance had planned to fly its Vulcan rocket from Florida the same day, but a power interruption at the plant that pumps fuel into the rocket pushed that launch to Saturday, Nov. 14. That delay could make Saturday the bigger day. If Starship lifts off on time, its upper stage will circle Earth for nearly a full day and try to come home to Texas Saturday afternoon, just hours after Vulcan’s new window in Florida. What time is the SpaceX Starship launch? The window runs from a quarter to 6 until 7 p.m. ET. SpaceX will stream the full mission on its website and on X, starting about 30 minutes before liftoff and running until the ship returns. The company has warned that the schedule could change. What is the double catch, and why does it matter? About seven minutes after liftoff, the Super Heavy booster is due to fly back to Starbase. There, the giant tower nicknamed Mechazilla will try to grab it with its mechanical ‘chopsticks.’ SpaceX has caught boosters this way three times, but this would be the first catch of its newest V3 booster. The ship, known as Ship 42, will then orbit Earth up to 14 times at about 171 miles high and release 26 Starlink satellites. Three of those satellites carry cameras that could send down hours of live views. About 22 hours after launch, the ship will try something never attempted: flying back to the launch site to be caught by the tower. SpaceX says success would mark the first full recovery of an orbital launch system. A fully reusable rocket could cut costs, and that matters because NASA is counting on Starship for future Artemis moon landings. What could still stop the launch? This is the part few people are watching. Bringing the ship home means flying it back over populated areas, which requires an updated license from the Federal Aviation Administration, according to NASASpaceflight. No approval had been publicly announced as of Thursday. Add weather and hardware, and Starship dates slip often. Why was ULA’s Vulcan launch delayed? Vulcan’s new 29 minute window opens just after half past noon ET Saturday at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station. The rocket carries 40 Amazon Leo satellites, the most Amazon has ever launched at once. That will push the constellation past 400 and further into competition with SpaceX’s Starlink , which has more than 11,000 satellites in orbit. It is also Vulcan’s first flight since an anomaly in February grounded it, and its first time flying with all six side boosters, for 3.9 million pounds of thrust. Musk and Jeff Bezos are now racing in the same sky, one weekend apart by a few hours. Why should everyday people care? Space can feel like a billionaires’ playground. But satellite internet is aimed at places where broadband never showed up, including rural communities across the South where Black families have waited years for reliable service. The ripple goes beyond Wi Fi. Earlier this year, Artemis II carried Victor Glover around the moon, making him the first Black astronaut to travel beyond low Earth orbit. Starship is the lander NASA needs for the Artemis missions that follow. Kids who watched Glover fly have a real reason to watch this one too. Friday the 13th gets the liftoff. Saturday could get the history. Whether Ship 42 makes it home is the cliffhanger nobody can call yet. records.title: SpaceX’s Starship returns to launch pad from orbit in victory for company
records.excerpt: SpaceX’s Starship returns to launch pad from orbit in victory for company | SpaceX | The Guardian Skip to main content Skip to navigation Print subscriptions Newsletters Sign in SpaceX's Starship returns to its launch pad and is caught by launch pad arms, following a test flight from Starbase in Texas, on Saturday. Photograph: Eric Gay/AP SpaceX's Starship returns to its launch pad and is caught by launch pad arms, following a test flight from Starbase in Texas, on Saturday. Photograph: Eric Gay/AP SpaceX’s Starship returns to launch pad from orbit in victory for company Although booster exploded, company caught upper stage for first time in campaign to make megarocket reusable SpaceX’s megarocket Starship returned to its Texas launch tower on Saturday, a milestone in the company’s efforts to make the craft suitable for human spaceflight. The 171ft (52-meter) bullet-shaped upper stage descended into the clutch of the tower’s mechanical arms, ending a 22hr mission where the craft orbited Earth 14 times. Starship’s 15th test flight was envisioned as a historic double-catch mission, where all parts of the rocket would be returned intact to the launch site, rather than recovered from the ocean as with some previous test flights. The hulking spacecraft is composed of two parts: a lower booster stage called Super Heavy, whose Raptor engines powered the orbital ascent, and an upper stage also called Starship. Those double-catch ambitions were dashed on Friday, when the booster diverted a few minutes after takeoff and exploded in the Gulf of Mexico. The guidance, navigation and control (GNC) system triggered the no-go. “It was doing what it was supposed to do. Basically, it detected that the booster was not in the place it was supposed to be to proceed with a catch,” SpaceX spokesperson Dan Huot said early on Saturday. The booster was also “slightly low on fuel”, according to SpaceX chief executive Elon Musk. This week’s test flight was still a victory for SpaceX , marking the first time that the company caught its upper stage. It was also only the second time Starship has entered Earth’s orbit. The feat comes as the 2028 date nears for Nasa’s plan to return humans to the lunar surface. The agency has contracted SpaceX and Jeff Bezos’s Blue Origin for the mission. “Making more believers by the day,” wrote Nasa administrator Jared Isaacman on X, praising the 15th flight. “One step closer to [the moon].” Isaacman is an ally of Musk, who advised Donald Trump to appoint him to lead Nasa. SpaceX has plans to ramp up its Starship test flights to a weekly, then twice-weekly cadence, Musk said on a recent earnings call. He has sought to make Starship rapidly reusable so that it can land and take off much like standard airplanes. Musk has touted the rocket’s reusability as a way to reel in the enormous costs of space travel. Beyond another Moon landing, Musk has also pushed a plan of carrying humans to Mars. Starship’s advances have also aided the expansion of Musk’s satellite internet empire. The spacecraft deployed 26 Starlink V3 satellites during this recent flight. records.title: SpaceX's giant rocket may leave NASA in the dust
records.excerpt: As it races to develop its new massive rocket, the space launch company is preparing to retire NASA's main ride to the International Space Station. Space SpaceX's giant rocket may leave NASA in the dust Updated November 13, 2026 12:14 PM ET Originally published November 13, 2026 5:00 AM ET Geoff Brumfiel SpaceX’s giant rocket may leave NASA in the dust Listen · 3:44 3:44 Transcript Download Embed < iframe src="https://www.npr.org/player/embed/nx-s1-6039312/nx-s1-10002726" width="100%" height="290" frameborder="0" scrolling="no" title="NPR embedded audio player"> Transcript SpaceX's mega rocket Starship makes a test flight from Starbase, Texas, Monday, Sept. 28, 2026. Starship is the largest rocket ever built, but it can't yet carry astronauts. Eric Gay/AP hide caption Eric Gay/AP Later today, SpaceX is planning the most ambitious test yet of its massive new rocket Starship. If all goes well, it will lift off from a pad in South Texas, circle the Earth and then land vertically at the same pad 22 and a half hours later. Space New space station crew launches from Florida on SpaceX's Crew Dragon capsule The test would be a major milestone for a rocket that company founder Elon Musk says he hopes will one day carry astronauts to Mars. But experts say the rapid development of Starship could also end up stranding one of the company's biggest boosters over the years: NASA. Space NASA chief blasts Boeing, space agency for failed Starliner astronaut mission That's because as SpaceX ramps up its new rocket, it has said it will stop flying a much smaller one called Falcon 9. Falcon 9 launches the company's Dragon capsule, which is currently the only American spacecraft capable of ferrying NASA astronauts to and from the International Space Station. "Because Dragon has become such a successful and reliable vehicle, it became the de facto way for astronauts to get to orbit," said Caleb Henry, director of research at Quilty Space, a firm that tracks the space industry. According to a NASA announcement in September, the space agency has contracted with SpaceX for three additional flights to the International Space Station. That would only allow Dragon to fly through 2028, assuming the missions were flown consecutively in six month increments and no further flights are contracted with SpaceX. SpaceX President Gwynne Shotwell has compared the Dragon Capsule to a minivan. "The road trip to Mars is six months — so you don't want to be in the minivan," she said. "We definitely want to move from the older technology to the newer technology." TIMOTHY A. CLARY/AFP via Getty Images hide caption TIMOTHY A. CLARY/AFP via Getty Images Space SpaceX's Starship launches on first orbital mission from Texas "NASA and SpaceX continue to work closely together across numerous missions and contractual agreements, including crew and cargo transportation to the International Space Station," the space agency said in an e-mail statement to NPR. "As the commercial space industry evolves, so will the technologies and services available to NASA." The space station is currently set to retire in 2030. "I love you guys" The current problem facing the space agency marks a stark reversal from earlier times, when it was SpaceX that was depending heavily on NASA. In 2008, following multiple failures of the Falcon 9, the space launch company was on the ropes. Space 4 people on NASA's Crew-12 mission return to Earth after 8 months in space "We were running on fumes at that point, we had virtually no money," Elon Musk told CBS' 60 Minutes in a 2014 interview. Then, just days before Christmas, NASA came through with a big contract. "I couldn't even hold the phone, I just blurted out, 'I love you guys!'," Musk said. Science With no crew aboard, spacecraft Starliner lands without a hitch For the next decade, a steady diet of NASA and eventually Pentagon contracts were responsible for a big share of the company's revenue. But all that changed in 2020, when SpaceX launched a subscription satellite internet service called Starlink. Starlink subscriptions quickly eclipsed the money made from launching rockets. NASA's SpaceX Crew-13 crew members (L-R) CSA (Canadian Space Agency) astronaut Joshua Kutryk, NASA astronauts Luke Delaney and Jessica Watkins, and Roscosmos cosmonaut Sergey Teteryatnikov walk out of the Neil A. Armstrong Operations and Checkout Building ahead of the launch at Kennedy Space Center on October 01, 2026 in Cape Canaveral, Florida. SpaceX is currently the main ride for NASA astronauts trying to reach the ISS. Justin Sullivan/Getty Images North America hide caption Justin Sullivan/Getty Images North America Today, according to SpaceX's latest financial report , the company made around $2.1 billion in revenue from space launches through September of this year. By contrast, Starlink pulled in around $12.8 billion, while its rapidly growing AI business made around $10.9 billion. Winding down Falcon Starship is central to SpaceX's newer, larger businesses. The space launch company is already using it to send its new, powerful V3 satellites for Starlink into orbit. Further down the road, Musk has said he wants the rocket to deliver data centers to space. Space NASA delays next crew launch to buy time at the space station for troubled Starliner "Once Starship is flying reliably several times per week, it makes sense to shift super scarce SpaceX engineering and production resources to Starship to get launch rate to several times per day, which means winding down Falcon," Musk said on X earlier this year. "We definitely want to move from the older technology to the newer technology," SpaceX president Gwynne Shotwell said at the All In summit in Los Angeles in September. "A Falcon 9 with a Dragon capsule on top is like a minivan. … The road trip to Mars is six months — so you don't want to be in the minivan." The problem is that the minivan is perfect for taking astronauts on a short jaunt to the space station. In fact, it's currently the only American option for making the trip. Henry said building space capsules is time-consuming and expensive. And as it turns out NASA is about the only one willing to pay, making it a very small market for a company like the one SpaceX has become. "Today there is not a strong commercial market for human spaceflight," he said. Launch gap The retirement of the Falcon rocket will have huge impacts beyond human spaceflight. A recent analysis by Quilty Space finds that the commercial market may end up short by some 150 launches between now and 2030, and the Pentagon has reportedly been left scrambling to find rides for national security satellites. In a statement to NPR, the U.S. Space Force said it had secured Falcon 9 launches through 2028 and that it was "confident" other suppliers would be able to pick up the slack. None of that is likely to change SpaceX's mind, according to Tim Farrar, the president of TMF associates, a telecom analysis firm that tracks SpaceX. The company has grown far beyond its launch business, he said. "SpaceX has now got an enormous amount on its plate." In particular, "it's not making a lot of money out of NASA," he said. "Although it seems likely that the individual missions are profitable, they're small potatoes." It's still not clear when SpaceX will retire the Falcon 9 rocket. The company did not respond to NPR's request for comment, but in her public comments at the summit, Shotwell implied that a rival company, Boeing, could fly to the station instead. "Boeing has been paid, I think, probably more than we have been paid to develop their human capsule. So we're just going to let them have some business," she said. "They should fly their capsule." The Boeing capsule, known as the Starliner, has been beset by problems throughout its development.
